one per company and analysis day, written by bot analyze

g.text: .gitignore: of reports/, only reports/*/analysis/*.json is tracked
the design document, the viewer's theme

text.tspan: scripts/weekly.sh, Saturdays 10:00
refresh, screen, analyze, then publish;
each step only when the previous one succeeded

g.text: 2. site workflow, on every push to master
3. bot site: build the static viewer
index.html: all companies by margin of safety, descending, with the first one's detail
404.html: served by GitHub Pages for any missing path
robots.txt: keeps crawlers out of f/ and rows/
c/TICKER.html (newest) and c/TICKER/YYYY-MM-DD.html: list with detail
f/TICKER.html and f/TICKER/YYYY-MM-DD.html, the detail alone

text.tspan: collect every reports/*/analysis/*.json
none: nothing to publish, exit 0
detached worktree .cache/site-publish
reset to origin/master on every run, then cleaned;
only the sidecars are copied in
the checkout the script runs from is never committed
anything new to commit?
no: no commit, exit 0
commit chore(site): publish analyses YYYY-MM-DD
push to origin master
push fails: exit 1

g.text: One deploy at a time: a newer push cancels the running one.
7. upload the site directory as the Pages artifact
8. deploy job, after the build job: publish the artifact to GitHub Pages
Any failing step stops the workflow; nothing is deployed.
Architecture decision record (ADR) 0008 (Implemented): the viewer is read-only; it values nothing and runs no bot command.

text.tspan: bot site --out path [--reports-dir reports] [--base-url /]
base URL normalised to one leading and one trailing slash
output directory safe to empty?
refused when it is the reports directory or contains it,
exists and is not a directory,
or is not empty and has no .bot-site marker file
refused: exit code 2
else emptied (or created), marker written before any page
scan reports/*/analysis/*.json
date = the folder name, ticker = the file stem
grouped by ticker, newest analysis first
usable sidecar?
folder name a YYYY-MM-DD date, stem a ticker of 1 to 12 characters
from A–Z, 0–9, '.' and '-'
a JSON object with schema_version 1, analysis.ticker = the stem
no: skipped with a warning
does each analysis have every field the views read?
no: that analysis is skipped with a warning;
a company with none left is dropped
one list row per company, from its newest analysis:
ticker, name, verdict, margin of safety, price, intrinsic value,
story type, red and yellow flags, date
verdict, as a filter value
margin of safety (MoS) ≥ 1.3: undervalued; ≥ 1.0: fair; < 1.0: overvalued; none: na
list rows and the detail's verdict sentence: the verdict text the sidecar carries, read back
value line and grid cells: recomputed from their MoS

g.text: verdict counts: all = every company, then one count per verdict

text.tspan: for every filter × sort × direction
filters all, undervalued, fair, overvalued, na; sorts ticker, mos, date; directions asc, desc
keep the rows of the filter's verdict, then sort; ties by ticker ascending;
by mos: rows without a margin of safety always last
detail of one analysis: verdict sentence, price against intrinsic value,
assumptions with their sources in words, tornado, grid of verdicts,
narrative flags as pass, warning, fail or not evaluated,
discounted cash flow (DCF) table, sanity check, earlier analyses
render every page from the templates;
every link starts with the base URL; static assets copied

g.text: What a reader sees: a list of companies with a verdict filter (with counts) and sorts by ticker, margin of safety or date; picking a company opens its detail beside the list (assumptions with their sources, tornado, grid, flags); earlier analyses stay reachable by date.
